The key idea is to use a gradient-based optimization (BFGS) where individual elements are perturbed to reduce the maximum convolution value, while ensuring non-negativity and bounds (\([0, 1000]\)). The optimality condition is that the sequence is proportional to the square of any vector satisfying specific constraints, which leverages mathematical properties to lower \( J \).

We represent a candidate sequence as \( a = \alpha \cdot x \), where \( \alpha \) is a scalar and \( x \) is a vector chosen from the unit sphere at each step. The optimization seeks to minimize \( \|(a)_k\|^2 \) subject to \( \alpha^{-1} \text{full\_convolve}(\sqrt{\alpha} \cdot x) \leq 1 \), which ensures the convolution peak is normalized and focuses solely on the shape.
